issues.title: Test function missing REDIS_TEST wrapper
issues.description: The rule requires that all test functions and test-specific code in source files must be enclosed within #ifdef REDIS_TEST / #endif blocks, but the validateStoredKeyConversion function is a test/validation function that exists without the required preprocessor wrapper
issues.rule_name: Test Functions Must Be Wrapped in REDIS_TEST Preprocessor Blocks

issues.title: Stored-key used for lookup instead of extracted key in defragmentation
issues.description: In activeDefragHfieldAndUpdateRef, the code extracts the lookup key from the stored-key (Entry*) using dictStoredKey2Key but then passes the original stored-key pointer to dictFindLink. After the API refactoring, dictFindLink expects a lookup key, not a stored-key. This will cause hash mismatches and comparison failures, leading to dictFindLink returning NULL when it should find the entry. The serverAssert on the next line will then trigger, crashing the server during active defragmentation of hash fields.

issues.title: Wrong stored-key pointer used for dict lookup after keyDup
issues.description: In dictSetKeyAtLink when newItem is 0 and *link is NULL, the function attempts to find the link by calling dictFindLink with addedKey. However, addedKey is the result of keyDup (if keyDup is configured) or the original stored-key, and dictFindLink expects a lookup key. Additionally, after keyDup, addedKey may point to a newly allocated object with a different address than the original key in the dict, causing the lookup to fail even with pointer comparison. This will cause the assertion to fail, or worse, result in corrupted dict state if the assertion is disabled.

issues.title: Unused local variable triggers -Werror build failure
issues.description: A new local variable `key` is introduced but never used. This will typically produce an `-Wunused-variable` warning, which becomes a build error under `-Werror`, violating the requirement that the build compiles cleanly with warnings treated as errors.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
const void *key = dictStoredKey2Key(d, ptr);
    link = dictFindLink(d, ptr, NULL);

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14646 - Replace fragile dict stored-key API with getKeyId callback

structured_output.summary:
This PR removes the stateful `dictUseStoredKeyApi()` toggle and its `storedHashFunction`/`storedKeyCompare` callbacks. In their place it adds one `dictType.keyFromStoredKey` callback. Inside dict.c, every stored key is converted to a lookup key with `dictStoredKey2Key()` before it is hashed or compared, so hash and compare functions only ever see lookup keys. The db and expires dicts now use `kvGetKey` and an sds-vs-sds `dictSdsCompareKV`. Hash dicts need no callback, since `Entry*` is sds-compatible. That is why `hashTypeDelete` could drop its `isSdsField` flag. The design is a clear improvement and most call-site changes are mechanical and correct.

There is one blocking problem. `defrag.c` now calls `dictStoredKey2Key()`, which is `static` in dict.c and not declared in dict.h. On the default Linux jemalloc build (`HAVE_DEFRAG`), that is an implicit function declaration. GCC 14+ treats this as an error by default; older compilers instead fail at link time with an undefined reference. Separately, `dictSetKeyAtLink` now passes the stored key `addedKey` to `dictFindLink`, which expects a lookup key, so its fallback path breaks for kvobj dicts. There is also an unused static helper that triggers `-Wunused-function`.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The defrag.c change won't build on the default jemalloc configuration, because it calls a function that is static in dict.c. dictSetKeyAtLink also passes a stored key where a lookup key is required. Both should be fixed before merge.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, dict had two families of hash/compare callbacks. Callers had to set a per-dict flag (`useStoredKeyApi`) before and after any call that passed a stored object, such as a `kvobj*` or an `Entry*`, instead of a lookup key (`sds`). This was fragile because forgetting the toggle silently used the wrong hash function.

The PR replaces this with one optional `dictType.keyFromStoredKey` callback. Inside dict.c, `dictStoredKey2Key()` turns any stored key into its lookup key before hashing (rehash, insert) and before comparing against bucket entries (find, delete, two-phase unlink, find-for-insert). As a result, `hashFunction` and `keyCompare` only ever receive lookup keys. Public functions that take stored keys are marked with the no-op `__stored_key` annotation. The db and expires dicts use `kvGetKey`. Hash dicts don't set the callback, because `Entry*` points at its sds field.
steps: Start in dict.h: `storedHashFunction`, `storedKeyCompare` and the `useStoredKeyApi` bit are removed, `keyFromStoredKey` is added, and stored-key parameters are marked with the `__stored_key` macro.
In dict.c, `dictStoredKey2Key()` is the single conversion point. `dictGetHash()` now always calls `type->hashFunction` on a lookup key.
Lookup loops (`dictFindLinkInternal`, `dictGenericDelete`, `dictTwoPhaseUnlinkFind`, `dictFindLinkForInsert`) convert each visited bucket entry before calling `cmpFunc`.
Insert paths (`dictAddRaw`, `dictSetKeyAtLink` with newItem=1, and rehash) convert the incoming stored key before hashing or searching.
In server.c, dbDictType and dbExpiresDictType set `.keyFromStoredKey = kvGetKey`, and `dictSdsCompareKV` becomes a plain sds-vs-sds compare.
Callers (rdb.c, t_hash.c, kvstore.c, defrag.c, module.c) drop the toggles, and `hashTypeDelete` loses its `isSdsField` argument.

findings.title: defrag.c calls dictStoredKey2Key, which is static in dict.c: build fails with HAVE_DEFRAG
findings.fixPrompt: In src/defrag.c, `activeDefragHfieldAndUpdateRef` (around line 280) calls `dictStoredKey2Key()`, which is `static` in src/dict.c and not declared in dict.h. This breaks the build when HAVE_DEFRAG is defined: GCC 14+ rejects the implicit declaration, and older compilers fail at link time. The variable `key` is also unused. Remove the `const void *key = dictStoredKey2Key(d, ptr);` line. `dictFindLink(d, ptr, NULL)` is correct as-is, because hash dicts have no keyFromStoredKey and Entry* is sds-compatible. If an exported helper is really wanted, declare a non-static `dictStoredKey2Key` in dict.h instead, and use its result in the dictFindLink call.

findings.title: dictSetKeyAtLink passes a stored key (addedKey) to dictFindLink, which expects a lookup key
findings.fixPrompt: In src/dict.c, in `dictSetKeyAtLink` (around lines 913-916), the newItem==0 fallback calls `dictFindLink(d, addedKey, NULL)`. `addedKey` is a stored key (possibly keyDup'd), but dictFindLink requires a lookup key. For dicts with keyFromStoredKey set (dbDictType, which stores kvobj), this hashes and compares the wrong type and asserts. Change the call to `dictFindLink(d, dictStoredKey2Key(d, key), NULL)`, matching the newItem==1 branch a few lines above, which already converts with dictStoredKey2Key before dictFindLinkInternal.

findings.title: Unused static validateStoredKeyConversion triggers -Wunused-function
findings.fixPrompt: In src/dict.c lines 101-108, the static function `validateStoredKeyConversion` is never called, so it produces a -Wunused-function warning. Remove it entirely. If validation is desired, add a debugAssert that `dictStoredKey2Key(d, key) != NULL` inside dictAddRaw / dictSetKeyAtLink instead.

findings.title: Single conversion point removes a class of toggle bugs
findings.body:
Centralizing the conversion in `dictStoredKey2Key()` is a real robustness win. Every bucket walk (find, delete, two-phase unlink, find-for-insert) converts the visited entry, and every stored-key entry point (`dictAddRaw`, `dictSetKeyAtLink` with newItem=1, rehash) converts the incoming key. As a result, `hashFunction` and `keyCompare` only ever see lookup keys.

This removed a lot of error-prone toggle pairs in rdb.c, t_hash.c and kvstore.c. It also let `hashTypeDelete` drop its `isSdsField` flag safely: `entryHashDictType` doesn't need `keyFromStoredKey`, because `Entry*` already points at its sds field. Simplifying `dictSdsCompareKV` to a pure sds compare also makes the `memory_prefetch.c` change (passing `kvobjGetKey(kv)`) consistent.
